title: LLM-based Human Simulations Have Not Yet Been Reliable

bias_targets.methodology: Reviewing experiments in utility theory from existing literature to compare LLM and human responses regarding time discounting, loss assessment, and inequity aversion.
Synthesizing comparative studies that evaluate LLM accuracy and value alignment in Western (e.g., U.S.) versus non-Western contexts (e.g., Japan, South Africa).
Reviewing empirical evidence on the frequency of models generating gender-stereotypical behaviors and analyzing attack bias success rates compared to humans.
Analyzing literature on how the overrepresentation of certain professions and social groups in training data reduces diversity and creates unrealistic reasoning for underrepresented groups.
